overall_summary: Space and extreme cosmic phenomena—specifically bizarre exoplanet weather and mind-bending planetary conditions—are the undisputed growth drivers for FACTVERSE, consistently pulling in the highest views and engagement. Conversely, psychology-based content and common animal trivia are failing to capture audience interest, indicating a need to pivot fully toward cosmic mysteries and high-concept physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,007 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (719 views) represent the channel's peak performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme planetary conditions, focusing on highly visual, hostile environments in the universe.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (263 views) and 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' (302 views) outperformed standard trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate physics-based time dilation and evolutionary timeline anomalies into the content calendar.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs...' (71 views) consistently flopped.
weak_patterns.action: Halt production on general cognitive psychology and brain hacks unless tied to a massive cosmic or sci-fi mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (183 views) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) generated very low traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid entry-level animal facts that are already widely known on the internet; pivot instead to cinematic animal survival narratives if exploring biology.

next_video.reason: Aligns with the highly successful exoplanet weather trend ('Burning Ice' and 'Supersonic Rubies') and fits the optimal 18-second retention-friendly duration.

experiment: Test a high-stakes 'What-If' cosmic scenario short (e.g., 'What If a Speck of Dark Matter Hit Earth?') to see if the space audience's appetite for extreme physics can be successfully funneled into hypothetical narrative-driven storytelling.
